label: es-e7e1
change: OriginalDiagnosticNumber computes the VC80 power-of-ten tables (2 x 21 twelve-byte entries for 10^p and 10^-p, p = d*8^g) instead of holding them as copied hex: the top 64 significand bits are 10^±p rounded to the nearest 64-bit value (ties to even), the low 16 bits those of 10^±p rounded to 80 bits, with a small private natural-number arithmetic. tableHex stays as a computed view; a new engine test checks the computed bytes' SHA-256 against the DLL tables' recorded digest.

derivation.method: a Python check over the 42 removed entries before the Swift code: simple rounding to 80 bits matched 13 and 10 of 21 (differences of exactly 2^16), the two-part rule all 42
derivation.tablesSHA256: 13175ac4fec5e3602495c2164b80050d181c3d0f9b948e48dd524f367b8d5508 (504 bytes; the same digest docs/research/DIAGNOSTIC_NUMBERS.md recorded for the DLL's records)

publicSurface: OriginalDiagnosticNumber.tableHex: a computed static var (internal) instead of a stored literal

review.verdict: no correctness defect: the code computes the rule; a Python port of the Swift reproduced all 42 entries and matched Python integers in 3,000 random arithmetic cases
required: the engine test's two exact entries no longer as verbatim hex but derived from their significands and exponents (done)
docs/research/DIAGNOSTIC_NUMBERS.md: a dated new statement that the table is computed, the earlier paragraph kept (done)
adopted: powers written as d*8^g (the groups the scaling looks up)
the comments' wording (the DLL's byte layout; the negative powers' bounds)
notes: unreachable traps: shiftedLeft with a negative count, shiftedRight past the width, .value beyond 64 bits; none reachable with these inputs
first use estimated at a few ms in release (about 16.6k division steps), only behind the diagnostic flag 0x450bec (OriginalPostHUDNotices.swift:98): a cold path; not measured
